issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` is a coarse over-approximation that can match unrelated tokens like `1s` in URLs/strings or identifiers like `dims`.
issues.detail: The pre-filter accepts any digit followed by optional `m` and `s`, so substrings inside `url(foo1s.png)`, string literals, or identifier-internal sequences still enter valueParser. Correctness is preserved because the real parser runs after, but the speedup is partially eroded. Tightening with a word boundary (`\dm?s\b`) would express intent more precisely.

issues.description: Missing one-line comment naming the regex as a cheap pre-filter and its invariant.
issues.detail: All three reviewers want a brief comment on `HAS_TIME` explaining it is an over-approximation gate before the expensive valueParser path, and naming the invariant that any time value must contain a digit immediately preceding `s` or `ms`. Saves the next maintainer time and makes the optimization self-documenting.

issues.description: No benchmark numbers or regression test pinning the early-return behavior.
issues.detail: The PR ships a performance fix without before/after measurements in the changeset and without a test that guarantees the early-return doesn't skip a real violation (weird whitespace, case, vendor-prefixed values). A single regression test plus a perf note would lock this in. Not blocking.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-shaped optimization: a cheap regex pre-filter short-circuits the expensive valueParser path when no time token is present, correctness is preserved by the real parser running after, and the reordering after the early-return avoids needless `toLowerCase`/`unprefixed` work. Consensus verdict: ACCEPT with trivial fixups. The regex is a deliberate over-approximation that could be tightened (e.g. word boundary) and should carry a one-line comment naming it as a pre-filter. The PR would also benefit from a benchmark note and a regression test pinning the early-return behavior.
